definition: The erosion and modification of the ground beneath and around a snow patch, caused by freeze-thaw action, solifluction, and meltwater — a slow sculpting of the earth by lingering snow rather than by a glacier's bulk.
etymology: From Latin nix, nivis, meaning snow, the same root that gives us nival and niveous. Geographers coined it in the early twentieth century to name a process that had always been happening quietly under the snowfields — they simply needed a word precise enough to separate it from glaciation proper.
usage: In late November the hillside hollows begin their long nivation, each freeze and thaw loosening another grain of soil to be carried off when the melt finally comes in spring.
